The match was fiercely contested in the opening 20 minutes. Following a "cooling break," both sides received a yellow card each—England midfielder Elliot Anderson and Argentina centre-back Lisandro Martínez. Before half-time, nearly every whistle was met with cheers from the home fans and jeers directed at the visiting team's fouls.

The two sides went into half-time level, and after switching ends, the second half got underway. In the 55th minute, England's Anthony Gordon latched onto a pass and fired home to break the deadlock, giving England a 1:0 lead. England fans in attendance immediately erupted in wild celebrations.

Trailing Argentina quickly launched a counterattack, fashioning three crosses from the right wing within ten minutes, but all were blocked, drawing sighs from many Argentina supporters. In the 85th minute, Enzo Fernández met a Messi cross with a header to level the score at 1:1. Argentina fans immediately burst into drum-beating celebrations, with air horns sounding all around.

In stoppage time, in the 92nd minute, Messi provided an assist for Lautaro Martínez to seal the result, helping Argentina advance to the final once again, where they will face Spain for the World Cup title. Argentina fans in the stadium were on cloud nine again, and even after the referee blew the final whistle, supporters continued to embrace in celebration, with some holding up cardboard cutouts of Messi.

Argentina fan Ho, who has been a Messi supporter ever since the forward rose to prominence at Barcelona, was wearing the Argentina "two-star" number 10 jersey. He pointed out that this World Cup is Messi's last, so the team must strive to defend the title. He believes that amid the controversy surrounding Messi and the team throughout the tournament, rather than supporters arguing over every decision and fan, they should cherish the final chapter of Messi playing for the national team. He joked that he is young and fit, so staying up late is no problem for him—but he...

England fans had been singing "Football's coming home!" throughout the tournament, yet once again failed to bring football home. Deaken, who is studying in the UK and returned to Hong Kong during the summer holidays, turned up today draped in an England flag, cheering loudly with friends amid the intense battle. He said it was his first time watching football in a mall to soak up the atmosphere, and felt that although both sets of fans were very invested, they showed each other mutual respect and there were no heated clashes.

When the team you support loses, disappointment is inevitable. Deaken, who shares a name with England midfielder Declan Rice, felt that England had put in a fairly respectable performance in this match. Having been through two World Cups, he put it bluntly: "We've waited 60 years—wait another four, what's the big deal!"

Argentina will face Spain on the 20th, looking to defend the title; the third-place play-off on the 19th pits England against France.
